newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Japan boards Hong Kong protest boat - Taiwan radio.
newsitem.headline: Japan boards Hong Kong protest boat - Taiwan radio.

text.p: Japanese coast guards on Monday boarded a Hong Kong boat leading a protest flotilla challenging Tokyo's claim to an East China Sea archipelago and prepared arrest activists, Taiwan state radio said.

"The Japanese have boarded the Protect-the-Diaoyus and are ready to begin making arrests," the radio, quoting ship-to-shore radio contacts, said of the high seas confrontation near the uninhabited islands between Taiwan and Okinawa.

The 100-tonne Protect-the-Diaoyus was leading a 20-strong flotilla from Taiwan and Hong Kong that deliberately entered what Tokyo regards as its waters around the islands, claimed by Japan as the Senkakus and Taiwan and China as the Diaoyus.

The late-morning boarding about 15 nautical miles off the islands northeast of Taiwan came after some 60 Japanese patrol boats issued warnings for the protest flotilla to stay away and to make no attempt to land on the disputed islands.

Taiwan radio said another protest boat had made an emergency request to Taiwan to come the activists' assistance. Taiwan's armed forces had a spotter plane, three rescue helicopters, three frigates and nine patrol boats nearby at the ready.

Before they set sail from Taiwan on Sunday night, protest organisers pledged to defy Japan's claims to the waters around the islands and would not rule out the possibility of attempting a landing, something Tokyo vowed to thwart.
